name: Cado

attributes.attribute: named in some versions as Dahut's partner

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cado is a Breton mythological figure. He was a sea god or a sea monster of Brittany. He compelled the princess Dahut, a pagan woman, to dwell underwater beside him. The storm that followed destroyed the city of Ys. Parts of the legend name the Devil as a partner to Dahut. Cado also turns up in the tale of the princess Blondine. There he is a forgetful suitor. He abandons her after freeing her from her magician father.

okr.objective: Cado is a Breton sea god tied to the ruin of Ys.
